2.text: day of the observance, according to the time when the sea becomes navigable

3.text: along different parts of the coast-line.

4.text: In the morning of the chosen day, men and women gather before the

5.text: house of the boat-owner and go to the winter boat-support to get the boat.

6.text: The winter boat-support is constructed of heavy pieces of bone of whale planted

7.text: firmly high up on the shore; and there the boat rests the whole winter

8.text: through, firmly fastened to the cross-poles, and protected from snowstorms

9.text: and the attacks of hungry foxes.

10.text: The whole company sacrifice sausage of reindeer-meat to the sea; then

11.text: they bring the boat close to the house and put it on the ground, on its west

12.text: side, and again offer sacrifice of sausage in the “direction” of the sea. Then

13.text: the whole party go around the house, following the course of the sun. At

14.text: the head walks the oldest woman of the family, then follow the owner of the

15.text: boat, the steersman, the paddlers, and after them come the other participants.

16.text: It is considered important that the woman who walks in front shall really be

17.text: the oldest of all, and know the necessary details of the ceremony: therefore

18.text: families who have no such woman among their housemates often send to

19.text: their relatives, or even to another village, for one. Old men, on the contrary,

20.text: are not considered necessary for the ceremonial.

21.text: After the procession is arranged, it enters the house, and the people

22.text: take their places around and begin singing their tunes. The singing, accom-

23.text: panied with dancing and beating the drum, lasts several hours, and ends

24.text: with a shamanistic performance in the evening. On the next morning the boat

25.text: is taken back to the sea and put on the summer support, which stands close

26.text: to the water. This latter is of slight build, and made of wood; and it may be

27.text: carried from place to place, according to the needs of the landing. The

28.text: floats of the boat are taken along and placed within. On the next morning

29.text: the participants in the ceremony bring to the shore a great amout of food. This is

30.text: distributed among the guests, who, with their housemates and women, come by

31.text: boat-loads. A sacrifice is offered to the sea, and then the boat is launched to try

32.text: the first course of the year, which is necessarily short, and conducted with caution.

33.text: On the morning of the night when the boat is still lying at the side of the

34.text: house, there is performed a divination with lumps of tallow which were left for

35.text: the night in the boat. By the cracks found in them the people try to divine

36.text: whether the boat will have good luck in the pursuits of the next season,

37.text: especially in regard to the whale and the polar bear. Cracks resembling

38.text: marks left by scratching with nails foretell good fortune and prosperity.

39.text: Cracks resembling marks left by touching with the finger-tips augur bad luck

40.text: and even death. Divination with tallow is used by the Maritime Chukchee

41.text: on other occasions also. In the fall, when the boat is taken to the winter

42.text: supports, the Chukchee do not perform any particular ceremonial, arguing that

43.text: the great ceremonial of the fall answers for all such purposes.
